Yes—you should be able to spot it, assuming the app’s positions are accurate and there are no local obstructions.

The Moon is **30.6° above the horizon**, toward **azimuth 232°**—roughly southwest. That is high enough to be well clear of most haze near the horizon. At **58% illumination**, it should be a fairly conspicuous half-to-gibbous Moon, and its angular separation from the Sun is about **99°**, so it is nowhere near the Sun’s glare region.

The main challenge is the **bright daytime sky**: the Moon’s contrast will be much lower than at night. Look in the southwest, ideally using a building, tree, or your hand to block direct sunlight—but **do not look near the Sun or use binoculars/telescopes unless you are certain the Sun cannot enter the optics**. Give your eyes a minute and scan around the predicted position; once found, it should be visible to normal unaided eyesight.
